items.title: Clean energy outpaced global electricity demand growth in 2025, Ember finds

featured_image.name: The State of Clean Energy, in 10 Charts - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Clean energy generation outpaced global electricity demand growth for the first time in 2025, powered by record solar expansion in China and India, according to energy think tank Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, released on Monday.[1][2]

Clean power generation grew 887 terawatt hours last year, exceeding overall global electricity demand growth of 849 terawatt hours, the report found. Solar energy, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of the net rise in electricity demand, and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.[3][1]

items.title: Asian markets trade mixed as U.S.-Iran ceasefire set to expire Tuesday night

featured_image.name: Asian markets track Wall St down with Nvidia, US jobs in view

items.description:
Oil prices dipped and Asian stock markets traded in mixed fashion on Tuesday as uncertainty deepened over the fate of peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, with a two-week ceasefire set to expire Tuesday evening Eastern time.

Brent crude slipped 0.4% while U.S. benchmark crude fell 0.9% in early Asian trading, according to the Associated Press. The declines came as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic talks in Islamabad against rising tensions, including the U.S. Navy's recent seizure of an Iranian cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: LHC experiment finds high-significance crack in the Standard Model

items.title: Iraq, Syria reopen Rabia border crossing after 13 years
items.description: Iraq and Syria on Monday officially reopened the Rabia-Al Yarubiyah border crossing, restoring a trade and transit route that had been shuttered for nearly 13 years amid civil war and the rise of ISIS. The reopening makes all official border crossings between the two countries operational for the first time since conflict engulfed the region.

items.title: Apple names John Ternus CEO as Tim Cook shifts to chairman role

featured_image.name: Apple (AAPL) Names John Ternus as Next CEO, With Tim Cook ...

items.description:
Apple announced on Monday that John Ternus, the company's senior vice president of hardware engineering, will become its next chief executive officer effective September 1, replacing Tim Cook, who will transition to the role of executive chairman of the board. The move, approved unanimously by Apple's board of directors, caps months of intensifying succession speculation and marks only the third CEO transition in Apple's 50-year history.[1][2][3][4]

Cook will remain as CEO through the summer to work closely with Ternus on the handover. As executive chairman, Cook will continue to assist the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world. Arthur Levinson, Apple's non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, will become the board's lead independent director on the same date.[3][1]

items.title: Starmer admits misleading Parliament over Mandelson vetting scandal

featured_image.name: Britain's Starmer Admits Misleading Parliament Over ...

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer addressed a hostile House of Commons on Monday, admitting that he had misled Parliament over the failed security vetting of Lord Peter Mandelson — but insisted the error was inadvertent.[1][2][3]

Starmer told lawmakers he should never have appointed Mandelson as the United Kingdom's ambassador to Washington, acknowledging a catastrophic lapse that has now engulfed his premiership and drawn resignation calls from all major opposition parties.[4][5]
